APIKeyResponse.description:
Management representation. `key_prefix` is the non-secret display prefix;
the full secret is never stored, so it never appears here.
APIKeyResponse.title: APIKeyResponse

AdminStatus.description:
`GET /v1/admin/status` — whether the install still needs its first admin
and whether the caller holds a valid session cookie.
AdminStatus.title: AdminStatus

AnalyticsBucket.description:
One time bucket of the analytics window. Missing buckets are zero-filled.

Deliberate deviation from Node: this report serializes snake_case, matching
the rest of the Rust `/v1/logs` surface, instead of Node's camelCase.

AnalyticsReport.description:
The `GET /v1/logs/analytics` report. Field names and semantics follow the
Node `LogsLogic.getAnalytics` result, but snake_case rather than camelCase.
AnalyticsReport.title: AnalyticsReport

CallbackResponse.description: The JSON answer a finished callback returns.
CallbackResponse.title: CallbackResponse

CatalogModel.description:
A catalog entry: the OpenAI model fields plus the operator's favorite flag
and the custom-model marker Node adds in `MergeCustomModels`.
CatalogModel.title: CatalogModel

ConnectedProvider.description: The connected provider, echoed back so the client can show what was stored.

CreatedAPIKeyResponse.description: Creation response: the management fields plus the one-time full secret.
CreatedAPIKeyResponse.title: CreatedAPIKeyResponse

LiveModelQuotaItem.description: A specific rate-limit window or model quota entry.

LoginResponse.description:
The login answer of an authorization-code provider: the browser URL plus the
PKCE material the client echoes back on the callback.
LoginResponse.title: LoginResponse

ProviderConnectionView.description:
A connection as the detail response reports it. There is deliberately no
credential field: a stored API key never leaves the database.

ProviderEntry.description: A provider as the list, catalog, and detail routes describe it.

connections.description: Detail only; the list and catalog omit it like Node does.

round_robin.description: Whether requests rotate across this provider's accounts.

ProviderModel.description:
A model line in the detail response. Hidden and favorited models stay in the
list so the admin view can restore them; `GET /v1/models` is the route that
drops them.

ProviderProtocol.description:
The wire protocol a provider speaks, as the catalog and the provider-auth
responses report it.

Three variants, matching what the build actually serves. Node's
`ProviderProtocol` union also lists `gemini`, but that value is dead: its only
user was the `gemini_cli` provider deleted with `packages/providers/src/catalog.ts`.

ProviderStatus.description: Connection state of a provider driver.

UpdateAPIKeyInput.title: UpdateAPIKeyInput

UsageStatsReport.description:
The all-time usage totals served by `GET /v1/logs/stats` and carried by the
`usage.updated` event. The wire keys are snake_case, as documented in
`docs/api-v1-contract.md`, "Logs in the Rust build".

adminSession.description: The admin session cookie. It also satisfies API-key auth on the routes that accept it.
adminSession.name: srouter_admin_session

bearerAuth.description: The same API key in the `Authorization` header.

srouterApiKey.description: An SRouter API key. `Authorization: Bearer <key>` carries the same credential.
srouterApiKey.name: x-api-key

info.description: Multi-provider OpenAI and Anthropic compatible LLM gateway, as served by the Rust build (`server/`). One listener on `PORT` carries the API, the dashboard SPA, and the provider callbacks; there is no secondary OAuth listener. Every response uses snake_case field names (owner ruling 2026-10-07), and errors use the `{error:{message,type,code?,param?}}` envelope. Cloudflare Tunnel routes and `/v1/settings/fallbacks/*` are excluded from this build by owner ruling; they do not appear below and answer `404`.
info.title: SRouter API
